sample_plan.subpopulation_description: Three U.S. residents ages 0–4, including infants and preschoolers whose needs and activities are caregiver- and developmental-stage-shaped; no independent hobbies or literacy skills are presumed.
Two U.S. residents ages 5–7, very young children whose daily activities remain substantially shaped by caregivers and developmental stage; no independently pursued hobbies are prescribed.
Four U.S. residents ages 8–14, spanning school-age children through young teens, with needs and routines that can vary by development and caregiver support.
Three U.S. residents ages 15–17, older adolescents whose education, early work possibilities, and independence remain shaped by age and circumstance.
Three U.S. residents ages 18–24 who are employed; young adults may be balancing work, education, and increasing independence.
One U.S. resident exactly age 24 who is unemployed and actively seeking work; this is an eligible young adult within the 15–24 age band.
Three U.S. residents ages 25–34, adults spanning varied work, household, and community circumstances; this directive selects an optimistic, active profile with traditional culinary tastes.

One U.S. resident ages 25–34 with the specified multigenerational White non-Hispanic cultural-background profile; the profile is paired with the matching race-and-ethnicity category and local-community cultural influence.
One U.S. resident ages 25–34 with a multiracial cultural-background profile, paired with the matching two-or-more-races category and a layered sense of cultural belonging.
One employed U.S. resident ages 25–34 with an extreme novelty-seeking approach to new products; this is an illustrative edge profile, not a prevalence estimate.

Five U.S. residents ages 35–44, employed adults with an urban lifestyle; this directive samples a strongly conservative belief profile alongside distinct culinary, shopping, product, and health contrasts.

Five U.S. residents ages 45–54, employed adults with varied household and community circumstances; this directive provides a progressive belief contrast and distinct mild-food, in-store shopping, health, and product-attitude profiles.

Three U.S. residents ages 25–54, an adult age band with varied work and household circumstances; this directive contrasts pessimism, vegetarian culinary tastes, frequent household shopping, global cultural influences, sedentary lifestyle, and travel avoidance.
One U.S. resident ages 25–54 with a persistently apathetic or disengaged general attitude, included as an illustrative contrast among eligible adults.

One U.S. resident ages 55–59 who is an employed, highly accomplished scientific or scholarly specialist with advanced education; the profile also allows baking interest and a multicultural cultural influence.
One U.S. resident ages 55–59 with rare extreme health-related behavior and a highly restrictive or selective culinary profile; this is an illustrative edge case, not a prevalence estimate.
One U.S. resident ages 55–59 who follows a fully plant-based diet, favors environmentally preferable products, and has a minimalist lifestyle.

Three U.S. residents ages 60–64 who are employed; this directive includes a chronic-condition or disability management contrast, nearby travel, and family-centered routines without narrowing the age eligibility band.
One U.S. resident ages 65–74 who is not currently in the labor force, with the rare extreme antagonistic or cynical personality profile included as an illustrative edge case.
One U.S. resident ages 65–74 who is not currently in the labor force, with an unusually hostile and persistently closed-minded general attitude; this is an illustrative extreme profile.

One U.S. resident ages 65–74 who is not currently in the labor force and is politically disengaged or disillusioned; political affiliation remains unconstrained because disengagement is not a party label.
One employed U.S. resident ages 65–74 with extravagant shopping and consumption-oriented lifestyle profiles; this is an illustrative behavioral contrast, not a claim about age or income.

One U.S. resident ages 75–110 who is not currently in the labor force and has had little or interrupted access to formal schooling, with limited literacy or numeracy; this does not imply inability to communicate.
One U.S. resident ages 75–110 who is not currently in the labor force and feels culturally isolated or alienated; the profile is sampled separately from race, politics, and finances.
One U.S. resident ages 75–110 who is not currently in the labor force and has a rural lifestyle, with routines shaped by local networks and travel primarily limited to familiar surroundings.
One U.S. resident ages 75–110 who is not currently in the labor force, with convenient prepared-food preferences, heritage-cultural ties, an irregular routine, and a tendency to avoid shopping.
